To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the heterotaxy gene, Galnt11, is essential for ciliogenesis and that the Galnt11-mediated glycosylation of Notch1 is crucial to the determination of cilia types and laterality.

Galnt11, a glycosyl transferase gene, regulates the expression of Notch1, which in turn regulates the ratio between motile and sensory cilia in the left-right organizer, thus establishing laterality in vertebrates.

GALNT11, a glycosylating enzyme, is required to generate asymmetric Notch signalling in the left-right organizer of vertebrates and to specify motile and immobile cilia in a ratio that determines laterality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the body axis of the developing embryo is established.
the mechanisms underlying left-right patterning and the aetiology of human congenital heart disease, a leading cause of infant death in developed countries.
the development of the human embryo
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GALNT11 is a novel gene in left/right axis determination.
GALNT11 O- glycosylates the Notch receptor to regulate its function and thereby the cilia type at the vertebrate left-right organizer, which determines the laterality of the developing embryo.
GALNT11 is a crucial gene for the determination of motile versus immotile ciliary types, and that its loss causes heterotaxy by disrupting this balance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we identified a new mechanism for heterotaxy, a congenital disease of left-right asymmetry in humans, by showing that a gene that is mutated in some patients, galnt11, is required for the development of motile and sensory cilia in the left-right organizer of the frog Xenopus tropicalis.
Galnt11 is essential for the determination of motile and non-motile cilia, and for the establishment of the left-right body axis.
Galnt11 is a novel regulator of cilia type and that Galnt11 regulates the balance of cilia type in the Xenopus left-right organiser.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glycosylation enzyme GALN11 is required for normal cilia function at the left-right organiser, which is essential for normal laterality.
Galnt11 is a new player in left-right patterning.
we have identified a new mechanism that is important to determine left-right body plan.
